title: Lifting computations over a fixed configuration
statement: Let $\Gamma$ and $Q$ be types, let $\Gamma$ have decidable equality, and let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $N$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $Q$. Suppose its transition action is independent of the scanned input symbol, and no transition prescribes erasing a work-tape cell by writing a blank. Let $x$ be a $\Gamma$-word and $x'$ a Boolean word of the same length, let $D$ be a configuration on $x$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $N$ on $x'$. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the lifted machine from the configuration formed by lifting $c$ over $D$ for $t$ steps gives the configuration formed by lifting the result of running $N$ from $c$ for $t$ steps over $D$.
hypotheses_covered: An embedding of Boolean symbols into $\Gamma$

No transition writes a blank on a work tape
